text:
maria: quick q — we need guidance on OpenTelemetry SDK usage across our Python/Go/Rust inference services. do we standardize on services exporting OTLP to the collector or permit direct-to-backend?

tom: i'd prefer OTLP -> otelcol internal. keeps proto/versioning consistent and lets us centralize sampling, batching, and retention rules.

leila: +1 to collector. also we need consistent span semantics for model calls: attributes for model.name, model.version, input.tokens, output.tokens, kv_cache_hit=true/false. otherwise dashboards end up noisy.

omar: important: python + gunicorn pre-fork needs the exporter/client re-init in the child. otherwise traces drop. in python we do this in post_fork hook with `opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.BatchSpanProcessor`.

kai: small config snippet we should standardize in repo READMEs: ```
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otel-collector.internal:4317
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.02  # 2% default
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=inference,env=prod,team=platform
```

leila: for inference-specific spans, name them like `inference.request` and set `inference.model_id`, `inference.seq_length`, `inference.kv_cache_hits`. use span events for `model_fallback` and `quantization_applied`. makes querying in the console easier.

maria: what about language differences? Rust SDK lacks stable metrics export in some versions. do we instrument counters for token counts in code vs relying on SDK metrics?

tom: i vote manual counters in code for token counters and kv cache hits (atomics). SDK metrics across langs is still inconsistent. traces (spans) we use SDKs, metrics we push via a small internal lib that normalizes names.

omar: exporter choice: otlp/gRPC is efficient but some sandboxes only allow HTTP. recommend supporting OTLP/gRPC by default and fallback to OTLP/HTTP. our otelcol accepts both.

kai: sampling: uniform 2% sucks for short-lived errors. suggest parent-based + tail-sampler in collector to keep errors and anomalous latency. that keeps cluster cost down but retains signals for SLO alerts.

leila: can we also add a small token-level attribute for billing? e.g., `billing.tokens_consumed` so cost drilldowns match traces. not the raw prompt text.

maria: agreed — no PII or prompts in spans. only hashes if needed.

tom: testing note: run local otelcol with our pipeline config and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` pointing at localhost when developing. also use `otel-cli` for quick span pushes.

omar: multi-process + async exporters: for python async workers, prefer using `OTEL_PYTHON_TRACES_SAMPLER` envs + non-blocking exporters. avoid sync exporters in hot request path.

leila: rust folks: if SDK doesn't support batch exporter we built a tiny shim that buffers `SpanData` and flushes on capacity/time. will upstream later.

maria: rollout plan suggestion: 1) update platform libraries with standardized attribute names and env var docs, 2) deploy otelcol config (collector-based sampling/retention), 3) ship SDK init examples for each lang, 4) run a canary for 48h.

kai: lgtm. i'll draft a short PR template for repo maintainers to add the standard envs + example init.

tracebot: automated-check — found missing `resource.attributes` in service `inference-gpu-2` (dev). marking ticket #INT-724.

maria: thanks — i'll follow up on INT-724, and i'll add the attr table to the internal telemetry cookbook. :thumbsup:
